newsitem.title: USA: Legionnaires' disease kills two in Detroit suburbs.
newsitem.headline: Legionnaires' disease kills two in Detroit suburbs.

text.p: Health officials on Friday were investigating an outbreak of Legionnaires' disease that has left two people dead and eight hospitalized over the past week in Detroit's northwestern suburbs.

Carolyn Bird, chief of medical services for the Oakland County Health Division, said the danger of further spread of the disease had probably subsided, but several of the 10 patients infected with the legionella bacteria remained in critical condition at area hospitals.
Two women, one in her 80s and another 74, have died from the disease in the past week. Bird said the patients ranged in age from 26 to 87, with an average age of 69.

Officials believe they all inhaled the bacteria in a small area of Farmington and Farmington Hills, Michigan, on the last weekend of September. They suspect the source was a building air conditioning system in the area.
"We think that the outbreak is essentially over, but we're trying to identify what particular facility might have been the source," Bird said.
The legionella bacteria, first identified in the 1970s, is typically found in warm standing water, and can be injected into the air in tiny moisture droplets emitted by cooling equipment.
